Macros Manual examples/redis_publishing_pubsub.rs /// The channel an audit entry goes to is a property of the type. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "audit")] struct AuditEntry { kind: String, } #[subscriber(RedisPubSub::new("events"), reply)] async fn on_event(event: &Event) -> AuditEntry { AuditEntry { kind: event.kind.clone(), } } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("events", "0.1.0")).with_broker( RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379"), |b| { // A `PUBLISH` to the `audit` channel, in place of the default publisher's `XADD`. b.include(on_event).out_reply(Publish::new()) }, ) } examples/manual/redis_publishing_pubsub.rs /// The channel an audit entry goes to is a property of the type. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, Outgoing, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] #[outgoing(name = "audit")] struct AuditEntry { kind: String, } struct OnEvent; impl Handle<Event, AuditEntry> for OnEvent { fn handle( &self, event: &Event, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<AuditEntry, HandlerOutcome>> { ready(Ok(AuditEntry { kind: event.kind.clone(), })) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("events", "0.1.0")).with_broker( RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379"), |b| { let on_event = subscriber(RedisPubSub::new("events"), OnEvent); // A `PUBLISH` to the `audit` channel, in place of the default publisher's `XADD`. b.include(on_event.reply().build()) .out_reply(Publish::new()) }, ) }

RedisPubSub reads one channel; a message reaches only the subscribers connected when it is published, and nothing is settled. RedisPubSub::new("prices") subscribes to the channel prices with SUBSCRIBE. Every subscription of the channel receives every message, in this service and in any other. Redis keeps nothing: a message published while no subscription is connected is gone. After a dropped connection the subscription subscribes again, and the messages published while it was down are not delivered. An outcome settles nothing: an ack, a retry and a drop all report AckError::Unsupported, and the runtime logs a warning for each. A retry_after still comes back, as a copy the runtime publishes to the channel. A subscription holds the messages that arrive while its handler is busy in a buffer. RedisPubSubPattern reads every channel a glob matches, and PubSubMode chooses between classic and sharded delivery.

Every price published on prices while the service runs. Macros Manual examples/redis_pubsub.rs /// Every price published on `prices` while the service is subscribed. #[subscriber(RedisPubSub::new("prices"))] async fn on_price(tick: &Tick) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(symbol = %tick.symbol, tick.cents, "price"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/redis_pubsub.rs /// Every price published on `prices` while the service is subscribed. struct OnPrice; impl Handle<Tick> for OnPrice { fn handle( &self, tick: &Tick, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(symbol = %tick.symbol, tick.cents, "price"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn prices() -> RedisPubSub { RedisPubSub::new("prices") }

buffer sets how many messages a channel subscription holds while its handler is busy; past it the oldest is lost with a warning. Redis pushes every message to the subscription as soon as it is published, whether the handler is ready or not. The subscription keeps what arrives in a buffer until the handler reads it. Without the setting the buffer holds fred's default of 32 messages. When it is full, the oldest message is dropped, and the subscription logs a warning with the channel and the number of messages lost. A handler that has to absorb a burst sets a buffer as large as the burst. The room is reserved when the subscription opens, about 600 bytes per message whatever the payloads weigh, because fred sizes all eight notification channels of a client by it. RedisPubSubPattern::buffer sets the same for a pattern subscription.

Trades arrive in bursts, so their subscription holds up to 1024 of them. Macros Manual examples/redis_pubsub.rs /// A burst of trades waits in a buffer of 1024 messages while the handler works through it. #[subscriber(RedisPubSub::new("trades").buffer(nonzero!(1024)))] async fn on_trade(tick: &Tick) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(symbol = %tick.symbol, tick.cents, "trade"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/redis_pubsub.rs /// A burst of trades waits in a buffer of 1024 messages while the handler works through it. struct OnTrade; impl Handle<Tick> for OnTrade { fn handle( &self, tick: &Tick, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(symbol = %tick.symbol, tick.cents, "trade"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn trades() -> RedisPubSub { RedisPubSub::new("trades").buffer(nonzero!(1024)) }

RedisPubSubPattern reads every channel a glob matches; a retry copy needs a destination named at the mount site. RedisPubSubPattern::new("quotes.*") subscribes with PSUBSCRIBE. It reads quotes.eu, quotes.us and any other channel the glob matches, with the glob syntax of Redis. A channel needs no setup in Redis, so a channel first used after startup is read as well. The subscription's name is the glob itself. Patterns are classic Pub/Sub: sharded delivery has no pattern subscription, and the descriptor takes no mode. A handler reads the channel a delivery came on through the Channel key of PubSubContext. A glob is not a channel a PUBLISH can name, so the descriptor offers no address for a retry copy. The registration names one with .out_retry(policy).to(channel), and a registration that names none does not start. The rest of the channel semantics are those of RedisPubSub: nothing is kept and nothing is settled.

The handler reads every quotes.* channel. Macros Manual examples/redis_pubsub.rs /// Every channel whose name matches `quotes.*`: `quotes.eu`, `quotes.us` and any added later. #[subscriber(RedisPubSubPattern::new("quotes.*"))] async fn on_quote(tick: &Tick) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(symbol = %tick.symbol, tick.cents, "quote"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/redis_pubsub.rs /// Every channel whose name matches `quotes.*`: `quotes.eu`, `quotes.us` and any added later. struct OnQuote; impl Handle<Tick> for OnQuote { fn handle( &self, tick: &Tick, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(symbol = %tick.symbol, tick.cents, "quote"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn quotes() -> RedisPubSubPattern { RedisPubSubPattern::new("quotes.*") } Its registration names quotes.retry for retry copies, a channel the glob matches, so a copy comes back to the same handler. Macros Manual examples/redis_pubsub.rs #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("market", "0.1.0")).with_broker( RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379"), |b| { b.include(on_price) // A glob is not a channel a `PUBLISH` can name, so the registration names the one // a retry copy goes to. The pattern matches it, so the copy comes back here. .include(on_quote) .out_retry(Publish::default()) .to("quotes.retry") .include(on_trade) }, ) } examples/manual/redis_pubsub.rs fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("market", "0.1.0")).with_broker( RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379"), |b| { b.include(subscriber(prices(), OnPrice).build()) // A glob is not a channel a `PUBLISH` can name, so the registration names the one // a retry copy goes to. The pattern matches it, so the copy comes back here. .include(subscriber(quotes(), OnQuote).build()) .out_retry(Publish::default()) .to("quotes.retry") .include(subscriber(trades(), OnTrade).build()) }, ) }

PubSubMode picks classic SUBSCRIBE and PUBLISH, broadcast to every node, or sharded SSUBSCRIBE and SPUBLISH, local to a slot. PubSubMode::Classic is the default. On a cluster a classic message travels to every node, so every node carries the traffic of every channel. It is the mode for standalone and sentinel servers, and the only one a pattern has. PubSubMode::Sharded needs Redis 7 or later. A sharded channel lives on the node that owns its hash slot, so its traffic stays there and a cluster scales with the number of channels. The two modes do not reach each other: a sharded subscriber hears only SPUBLISH, and a classic one only PUBLISH. So the subscription sets its mode with RedisPubSub::mode, and a publish policy aimed at it sets the same one with RedisPubSubPublish::mode. One service reads a channel in one mode: a second subscription that reads it in the other mode does not start.

Orders arrive on a sharded channel, and the shipment answering each one leaves with SPUBLISH to a sharded channel a tracker reads. Macros Manual examples/redis_pubsub_sharded.rs /// Reads `orders.eu` with `SSUBSCRIBE` and answers on `shipments.eu`. #[subscriber(RedisPubSub::new("orders.eu").mode(PubSubMode::Sharded), reply)] async fn ship(order: &Order) -> Shipment { tracing::info!(order.id, "shipping"); Shipment { order: order.id } } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shipping", "0.1.0")).with_broker( RedisBroker::cluster(["redis://localhost:7000"]), |b| { // The reply leaves with `SPUBLISH`: a sharded subscriber hears only a sharded publish. b.include(ship) .out_reply(Publish::new().mode(PubSubMode::Sharded)) .include(track) }, ) } examples/manual/redis_pubsub_sharded.rs /// Reads `orders.eu` with `SSUBSCRIBE` and answers on `shipments.eu`. struct Ship; impl Handle<Order, Shipment> for Ship { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Shipment, HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "shipping"); ready(Ok(Shipment { order: order.id })) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shipping", "0.1.0")).with_broker( RedisBroker::cluster(["redis://localhost:7000"]), |b| { let orders = RedisPubSub::new("orders.eu").mode(PubSubMode::Sharded); let shipments = RedisPubSub::new("shipments.eu").mode(PubSubMode::Sharded); // The reply leaves with `SPUBLISH`: a sharded subscriber hears only a sharded publish. b.include(subscriber(orders, Ship).reply().build()) .out_reply(Publish::new().mode(PubSubMode::Sharded)) .include(subscriber(shipments, Track).build()) }, ) }

RedisStream::new reads fresh entries off a stream through a consumer group, and each ack is an XACK. The read is XREADGROUP with the id >: entries no consumer of the group has been handed yet. group names the group, and a descriptor without one stops the service at startup. The subscription creates its group when it opens, with XGROUP CREATE ... MKSTREAM, so neither the group nor the stream has to exist first. Where a new group starts is its StreamStart. Every group reads every entry of the stream. The consumers of one group share its entries: each entry goes to one of them. consumer names this subscription's consumer; without it each subscription gets a unique generated name. An entry is handed out once and waits in the group's pending entries list until its handler settles it. An ack is XACK, which takes it off that list. An entry whose consumer died before settling stays there, and a reclaim or a claiming subscription takes it back. That makes a stream the recommended form for durable work: the server itself keeps what each consumer holds and how often it was delivered. A reliable list recovers the same work only through a recovery set that the service sweeps. The three constructors are the three read modes, because each returns a different set of entries. A stream keeps its entries until it is trimmed, so a group can be moved back over them or forward past them.

Billing and shipping read every order, each in its own group. Macros Manual examples/redis_streams_new.rs /// Bills every order, in the group `billing`. #[subscriber(RedisStream::new("orders").group("billing"))] async fn bill(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order billed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } /// Ships every order, in the group `shipping`: a second group reads the same entries again. #[subscriber(RedisStream::new("orders").group("shipping").consumer("shipping-1"))] async fn ship(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order shipped"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } fn app() -> impl App { let broker = RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(broker, |b| b.include(bill).include(ship)) } examples/manual/redis_streams_new.rs /// Bills every order. struct Bill; impl Handle<Order> for Bill { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order billed"); ready(Ok(())) } } /// Ships every order. struct Ship; impl Handle<Order> for Ship { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order shipped"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { let broker = RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { let billing = RedisStream::new("orders").group("billing"); // A second group reads the same entries again. let shipping = RedisStream::new("orders") .group("shipping") .consumer("shipping-1"); b.include(subscriber(billing, Bill).build()) .include(subscriber(shipping, Ship).build()) }) }

claiming reads pending entries idle at least min_idle and the fresh tail in one XREADGROUP ... CLAIM call; it needs Redis 8.4. The read takes the stale entries first, the longest idle first, and fills the rest with fresh ones. One subscription and one handler cover new work and recovery alike. min_idle has no default. Set it above the longest time a handler takes, or an entry a healthy consumer is still working on is taken over and handled twice. A retry leaves the entry in the pending entries list: nothing is appended, and the entry keeps its id. The same subscription reads it again once it has been idle min_idle. So a retry waits out min_idle, and a retry_after shorter than that waits min_idle too. Each delivery reports the attempts before it in the DELIVERY_COUNT_HEADER header, zero for an entry read off the tail, and its idle time in IDLE_MS_HEADER. A server older than 8.4 refuses the subscription, and the service does not start. The error, RedisError::ServerTooOld, names the subscription, the mode and both versions. On such a server the recovery is a reclaim subscription beside a new one.

An order out of stock stays pending and comes back after thirty seconds. Macros Manual examples/redis_streams_claiming.rs /// Fulfils new orders and the ones a worker took and never finished. An order out of stock stays /// pending, and the subscription takes it back once it has been idle 30 seconds. #[subscriber(RedisStream::claiming("orders", Duration::from_secs(30)).group("fulfilment"))] async fn fulfil(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { if !order.in_stock { tracing::warn!(order.id, "out of stock, the order comes back"); return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } tracing::info!(order.id, "order fulfilled"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/redis_streams_claiming.rs /// Fulfils new orders and the ones a worker took and never finished. An order out of stock stays /// pending, and the subscription takes it back once it has been idle 30 seconds. struct Fulfil; impl Handle<Order> for Fulfil { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { if !order.in_stock { tracing::warn!(order.id, "out of stock, the order comes back"); return ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::retry())); } tracing::info!(order.id, "order fulfilled"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app(url: &str) -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("fulfilment", "0.1.0")).with_broker( RedisBroker::standalone(url), |b| { let orders = RedisStream::claiming("orders", Duration::from_secs(30)).group("fulfilment"); b.include(subscriber(orders, Fulfil).build()) }, ) }

reclaim reads only entries another consumer of the group fetched and never acked, idle at least min_idle, with XAUTOCLAIM. It is the recovery path for a consumer that crashed or hung while it held entries. It runs as a second subscription on the same group, beside a RedisStream::new one that reads the fresh tail. A fresh entry is no one's unfinished work, so a reclaim subscription never reads it. min_idle has no default. Set it above the longest time a handler takes, or an entry a healthy consumer is still working on is taken over and handled twice. The subscription scans the pending entries list, and between two scans that found nothing it waits its block. A reclaimed delivery carries the server's count of its deliveries, this one included, in the DELIVERY_COUNT_HEADER header. A retry on a reclaim subscription appends a copy of the entry to the stream and acknowledges the original. On Redis 8.4 and later one claiming subscription covers both the fresh tail and the recovery.

A worker reads the fresh tail of orders, and a recovery handler of the same group takes back what a worker left pending for a minute. Macros Manual examples/redis_streams_reclaim.rs /// The worker: fresh entries off the tail of `orders`. #[subscriber(RedisStream::new("orders").group("workers"))] async fn work(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order processed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } /// The recovery path of the same group: entries a worker took and left unacknowledged for a /// minute, because it crashed or hung. #[subscriber(RedisStream::reclaim("orders", Duration::from_secs(60)).group("workers"))] async fn recover(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order recovered"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } fn app() -> impl App { let broker = RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(broker, |b| b.include(work).include(recover)) } examples/manual/redis_streams_reclaim.rs /// The worker: fresh entries off the tail of `orders`. struct Work; impl Handle<Order> for Work { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order processed"); ready(Ok(())) } } /// The recovery path: entries a worker took and left unacknowledged. struct Recover; impl Handle<Order> for Recover { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order recovered"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { let broker = RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { let fresh = RedisStream::new("orders").group("workers"); // Idle a minute: the worker that took it crashed or hung. let stale = RedisStream::reclaim("orders", Duration::from_secs(60)).group("workers"); b.include(subscriber(fresh, Work).build()) .include(subscriber(stale, Recover).build()) }) }

StreamStart says where a consumer group starts when the subscription creates it: the beginning, the end, or after an id. A descriptor names it with start_id. StreamStart::New is the default: the group reads only entries added after it was created. StreamStart::Beginning makes the group read every entry the stream still holds, then the new ones. StreamStart::Id(id) starts the group after that entry id, which it does not deliver. The setting is read once, when the group is created. A group that already exists keeps its own cursor, whatever a later start names. A group that has to move on every start is a start_at subscription.

A reporting group added to a running system reads the orders the stream already holds, the first time it is created. Macros Manual examples/redis_streams_start.rs /// A reporting group added to a running system: the first time it is created, it reads every /// order the stream still holds, then the new ones. #[subscriber(RedisStream::new("orders").group("reports").start_id(StreamStart::Beginning))] async fn report(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order reported"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/redis_streams_start.rs /// Reports every order it reads. struct Report; impl Handle<Order> for Report { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order reported"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { let broker = RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("reports", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { // The first time the group is created, it reads every order the stream still holds. let orders = RedisStream::new("orders") .group("reports") .start_id(StreamStart::Beginning); b.include(subscriber(orders, Report).build()) }) }

A key in #[subscriber] reads that stream through the broker's default group; a descriptor names the form and its settings. #[subscriber("orders")] reads the Redis stream orders. A stream is read only through a consumer group, and a bare key names none, so the group comes from RedisBroker::default_group. A bare key on a broker with no default group stops the service at startup, and the error names the setting and the key. Every other subscription is a descriptor, written where the key goes, as the attribute's first argument. One descriptor is one form of delivery and carries all of that form's settings: Form Descriptor What one subscription reads Stream RedisStream entries of a stream, through a consumer group List RedisList elements popped off a list, each by one consumer Channel RedisPubSub messages published to a channel while it listens Pattern RedisPubSubPattern messages of every channel a glob matches The manual form passes the key, or the descriptor itself, to subscriber(source, body). Each subscription reads on a connection of its own, beside the pool that publishes and settles. The settings of the mount chain apply to every form: the batch size, the dispatch lanes, the retry cap, the publishers. block is the one Redis setting among them.

The stream orders, read in the group workers. Macros Manual examples/redis_subscriptions_name.rs /// Reads the stream `orders`; the consumer group comes from the broker. #[subscriber("orders")] async fn place(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order placed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } fn app() -> impl App { let broker = RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379").default_group("workers"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| b.include(place)) } examples/manual/redis_subscriptions_name.rs /// Reads the stream `orders`; the consumer group comes from the broker. struct Place; impl Handle<Order> for Place { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order placed"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { let broker = RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379").default_group("workers"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(broker, |b| b.include(subscriber("orders", Place).build())) }

A slice handler reads one XREADGROUP COUNT on a stream; a list or a channel builds its batch on the client up to the same size. A handler over &[T] is a batch handler, and batch(n) at the mount site is its largest batch. The step is required on a slice handler: mounting one without it does not compile. A single-message handler does not offer the step at all; its concurrency is workers(n). On a stream the size is the COUNT of the read that fetches the batch, XREADGROUP or XAUTOCLAIM. The server sends at most n entries, and the handler gets exactly what one read returned, never an empty batch. A list and a channel deliver one value at a time. Their subscriptions gather a batch on the client from the values already waiting, up to the same n, and hand it over without waiting for more. So a batch is often smaller than n, and a quiet key yields batches of one. One outcome settles every entry of the batch. In the manual form the body is an impl Handle<[T]>, where Ok(()) settles the batch with an ack and Err(outcomes) settles entry i with outcome i. A stream batch reads a StreamBatchContext, which carries the group and its seek handle and no field of one entry. The block step chains after the size.

Three values waiting on each form arrive in one call. The stream handler and the app: Macros Manual examples/redis_subscriptions_batches.rs /// Bills the orders one read returned, at most 16. #[subscriber(RedisStream::new("orders").group("billing"))] async fn bill(orders: &[Order]) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(count = orders.len(), "orders billed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { let broker = RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("billing", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(bill.batch(nonzero!(16))) .include(pack.batch(nonzero!(16))) .include(count.batch(nonzero!(16))) }) } examples/manual/redis_subscriptions_batches.rs /// Bills the orders one read returned. struct Bill; impl Handle<[Order]> for Bill { fn handle( &self, orders: &[Order], _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), Vec<HandlerOutcome>>> { tracing::info!(count = orders.len(), "orders billed"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { let broker = RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("billing", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { let orders = RedisStream::new("orders").group("billing"); b.include(subscriber(orders, Bill).batch(nonzero!(16)).build()) .include( subscriber(RedisList::new("jobs"), Pack) .batch(nonzero!(16)) .build(), ) .include( subscriber(RedisPubSub::new("clicks"), Count) .batch(nonzero!(16)) .build(), ) }) } The list and the channel handlers: Macros Manual examples/redis_subscriptions_batches.rs /// Packs the jobs waiting on the list `jobs`, at most 16 at once. #[subscriber(RedisList::new("jobs"))] async fn pack(jobs: &[Order]) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(count = jobs.len(), "jobs packed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } /// Counts the clicks heard on the channel `clicks`, at most 16 at once. #[subscriber(RedisPubSub::new("clicks"))] async fn count(clicks: &[Order]) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(count = clicks.len(), "clicks counted"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/redis_subscriptions_batches.rs /// Packs the jobs waiting on the list `jobs`. struct Pack; impl Handle<[Order]> for Pack { fn handle( &self, jobs: &[Order], _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), Vec<HandlerOutcome>>> { tracing::info!(count = jobs.len(), "jobs packed"); ready(Ok(())) } } /// Counts the clicks heard on the channel `clicks`. struct Count; impl Handle<[Order]> for Count { fn handle( &self, clicks: &[Order], _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), Vec<HandlerOutcome>>> { tracing::info!(count = clicks.len(), "clicks counted"); ready(Ok(())) } }

block sets how long one read waits on the server: the XREADGROUP BLOCK on a stream, the BRPOP or BLMOVE timeout on a list. The wait is five seconds unless a subscription names another. A descriptor names it with RedisStream::block or RedisList::block. The mount site names it with the block step, which overrides the descriptor. The step chains after another step of the mount chain: after .batch(n), after .pipeline(), or, in the manual form, after build(). It reads the same before and after start_at(..). On a reclaim subscription the wait is the pause between two XAUTOCLAIM scans that found nothing. A read wakes as soon as an entry arrives, so the wait costs nothing on a busy stream. It decides how soon an idle read sees what happens beside it: a seek of its group, or a due entry of a delay queue, which the subscription sweeps once per read. A shorter wait sees them sooner, at the price of one more round trip per idle wait. The step exists on stream and list subscriptions, the two forms whose read blocks.

Orders wait at most a second per read; invoices are billed sixteen at a time, with a two-second wait set at the mount site. Macros Manual examples/redis_subscriptions_block.rs /// Each read of `orders` waits at most one second on the server. #[subscriber(RedisStream::new("orders").group("workers").block(Duration::from_secs(1)))] async fn place(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order placed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } /// Bills up to 16 orders a read. #[subscriber(RedisStream::new("invoices").group("billing"))] async fn bill(orders: &[Order]) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(count = orders.len(), "orders billed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } fn app() -> impl App { let broker = RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(place) // The size is the framework's step and the wait is Redis's, chained after it. .include(bill.batch(nonzero!(16)).block(Duration::from_secs(2))) }) } examples/manual/redis_subscriptions_block.rs /// Places one order. struct Place; impl Handle<Order> for Place { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order placed"); ready(Ok(())) } } /// Bills the orders of one read. struct Bill; impl Handle<[Order]> for Bill { fn handle( &self, orders: &[Order], _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), Vec<HandlerOutcome>>> { tracing::info!(count = orders.len(), "orders billed"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { let broker = RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { // Each read of `orders` waits at most one second on the server. let orders = RedisStream::new("orders") .group("workers") .block(Duration::from_secs(1)); let invoices = RedisStream::new("invoices").group("billing"); b.include(subscriber(orders, Place).build()).include( subscriber(invoices, Bill) .batch(nonzero!(16)) .build() .block(Duration::from_secs(2)), ) }) }

An envelope is how a message's headers travel beside its payload; the broker names one, and a descriptor or a publish policy names its own. A list element and a channel message are one value, and a stream entry is a map of fields. An envelope is the layout of the headers and the payload in them. RedisBroker::envelope sets the broker's envelope, and every subscription and publish policy uses it unless it names its own. A subscription names its own at the mount site with RedisEnvelopeExt::envelope: b.include(handler.envelope(FastStream)). On the manual path the descriptor names it: RedisList::new("jobs").envelope(FastStream). A publish policy names its own with envelope(..): RedisListPublish::new().envelope(FastStream). The envelope is a type, so the choice costs nothing per message. A delivery finds its payload without reading the headers, and reads them the first time a handler asks. A header block that does not parse reads as no headers, and the subscription logs a warning; a handler that requires a header then meets the ordinary missing-header error. Envelope List element, channel message Stream entry envelope::RustStream, the default a binary frame that opens with a marker; a message without headers is its bare payload the payload in _payload, each header in h:<name> FastStream faststream's BinaryMessageFormatV1 the same frame in __data__ Framed a {headers, payload} document written by a codec, its payload in CloudEvents' convention the document in _payload NoOp the payload alone the payload in _payload envelope::RustStream writes the bytes every earlier release wrote, so services on different releases read each other. A binary frame written by 0.7.1 or an earlier release has no marker and reads as its payload, frame bytes included, so services that share a list or a channel upgrade together. FastStream shares lists, channels and streams with a faststream service in both directions. Its header names travel as they are, so faststream's own headers arrive as correlation_id and reply_to. Framed with JsonCodec writes text that redis-cli and RedisInsight show as it is. Its payload follows the convention of CloudEvents' JSON format. A payload that is a JSON text is embedded as the value it is and reads back byte for byte: {"headers":{"event":"created"},"payload":{"id":7}}. Any other payload travels as standard base64: {"headers":{"event":"created"},"payload_base64":"CAc="}. With CBOR, msgpack or a codec of the service's own the payload is a byte string in payload; the codec implements FrameCodec, which this crate's json, cbor and msgpack features do for the framework's codecs. A header is a text field, and a header whose value is not text refuses the publish. The document of the codec(..) framing of 0.7.2 and earlier releases carried its payload as a string, so Framed reads it as a JSON string; services that share such a list switch together, and the list is drained first. A value that is not one of the envelope's own arrives as the payload with no headers, whatever its first bytes are. A stream entry without the envelope's field arrives as one JSON object of its fields. A payload that only looks like an envelope is written so that it reads back unchanged. A subscription and the publishers that write its name use one envelope. The broker's default publisher, which writes a retry copy and a reply that name no policy, writes the broker's envelope and the built-in ones. A subscription that reads through an envelope of the service's own, on a broker with another one, has its retry copies published through a policy that names it, out_retry(Publish::new().envelope(MyEnvelope)); the default publisher refuses that name, and the error names it. Two subscriptions that read one name through different envelopes stop the service at startup. NoOp has no room for headers, so a delivery read through it carries none of the message's. The headers a stream read itself reports, the delivery count and the idle time of a claiming read, stay. A publish through it that carries a header fails, and the error names the header and the destination. A retry copy the runtime publishes carries its retry count in a header, so a retry through NoOp fails the same way.

A faststream shop appends orders to a stream, and the broker reads its frame. Jobs go to a list as JSON documents, and a price feed publishes bare JSON. Macros Manual examples/redis_subscriptions_envelopes.rs /// The list jobs leave through. #[derive(OutSlot)] #[publishes(Job)] struct Jobs; /// Reads the orders a faststream shop appends, in the broker's envelope, and queues a job for /// each with the tenant in a header. #[subscriber(RedisStream::new("orders").group("dispatch"))] async fn dispatch(order: &Order, Out(jobs): Out<impl Publisher, Jobs>) -> HandlerOutcome { let mut headers = HeaderMap::new(); headers.insert("tenant", order.tenant.clone()); let job = Job { order: order.id }; if jobs .message(&job) .with_headers(headers) .publish() .await .is_err() { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } HandlerOutcome::ack() } /// Runs each job for the tenant its header names; the list holds JSON documents. #[subscriber(RedisList::new("jobs"))] async fn run(job: &Job, ctx: &mut Context<'_>) -> HandlerOutcome { let Some(tenant) = ctx.headers().get_str("tenant") else { tracing::warn!(job.order, "a job without a tenant is dropped"); return HandlerOutcome::drop(); }; tracing::info!(job.order, tenant, "job run"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } /// Reads the prices a feed publishes as bare JSON, with no headers. #[subscriber(RedisPubSub::new("prices"))] async fn on_price(price: &Price) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(price.sku, price.cents, "price"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } fn app() -> impl App { // faststream's frame wherever nothing names another envelope. let broker = RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379").envelope(FastStream); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("jobs", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { // Both ends of `jobs` name JSON, so `redis-cli` and RedisInsight show each job as text. b.include(dispatch) .out( Jobs, RedisListPublish::new().envelope(Framed::new(JsonCodec)), ) .build() .include(run.envelope(Framed::new(JsonCodec))) .include(on_price.envelope(NoOp)) }) } examples/manual/redis_subscriptions_envelopes.rs /// The list jobs leave through. struct Jobs; impl OutSlot for Jobs { const NAME: &'static str = "Jobs"; // `Job` fixes its destination, so no transform on this slot may name one. type Destination = Reads; } impl PublishedThrough<Jobs> for Job {} /// Reads the orders a faststream shop appends, in the broker's envelope, and queues a job for /// each with the tenant in a header. struct Dispatch; impl<Entry> Handle<Order, (), Outs<(Entry,)>> for Dispatch where Entry: OutEntry<Jobs, Wire: Publisher>, { async fn handle( &self, order: &Order, outs: &Outs<(Entry,)>, _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let mut headers = HeaderMap::new(); headers.insert("tenant", order.tenant.clone()); let job = Job { order: order.id }; outs.get(Jobs) .message(&job) .with_headers(headers) .publish() .await .map_err(|_| HandlerOutcome::retry()) } } /// Runs each job for the tenant its header names; the list holds JSON documents. struct Run; impl Handle<Job> for Run { fn handle( &self, job: &Job, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { let Some(tenant) = ctx.headers().get_str("tenant") else { tracing::warn!(job.order, "a job without a tenant is dropped"); return ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::drop())); }; tracing::info!(job.order, tenant, "job run"); ready(Ok(())) } } /// Reads the prices a feed publishes as bare JSON, with no headers. struct OnPrice; impl Handle<Price> for OnPrice { fn handle( &self, price: &Price, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(price.sku, price.cents, "price"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { // faststream's frame wherever nothing names another envelope. let broker = RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379").envelope(FastStream); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("jobs", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { let orders = RedisStream::new("orders").group("dispatch"); let jobs = RedisList::new("jobs").envelope(Framed::new(JsonCodec)); let prices = RedisPubSub::new("prices").envelope(NoOp); // Both ends of `jobs` name JSON, so `redis-cli` and RedisInsight show each job as text. b.include(subscriber(orders, Dispatch).build()) .out( Jobs, RedisListPublish::new().envelope(Framed::new(JsonCodec)), ) .build() .include(subscriber(jobs, Run).build()) .include(subscriber(prices, OnPrice).build()) }) }

An envelope of the service's own implements Envelope. locate finds the payload in a value, headers reads the headers, and seal writes a message. A stream entry keeps the sealed value in _payload unless the envelope overrides entry_field or the other entry methods. A broker whose own envelope is one of the service's own, or Framed over a codec of the service's, registers itself with the test harness beside the tests: ruststream::register_testable_broker!(RedisBroker<MyEnvelope>);. Macros Manual examples/redis_subscriptions_envelopes.rs /// One JSON line with the headers under `meta` and the payload as text under `body`: the layout /// a legacy system on the same list writes. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)] struct MetaLine; #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)] struct Line { meta: BTreeMap<String, String>, body: String, } impl Envelope for MetaLine { const CONTENT_TYPE: &'static str = "application/json"; fn locate(&self, value: &[u8]) -> Location { serde_json::from_slice::<Line>(value).map_or(Location::Bare, |line| { Location::Decoded(line.body.into_bytes()) }) } fn headers(&self, value: &[u8]) -> Option<HeaderMap> { let line = serde_json::from_slice::<Line>(value).ok()?; let mut headers = HeaderMap::new(); for (name, text) in line.meta { headers.insert(name, text); } Some(headers) } fn seal( &self, payload: &[u8], headers: &HeaderMap, value: &mut Vec<u8>, ) -> Result<(), SealError> { let line = Line { meta: headers .iter() .map(|(name, text)| (name.to_owned(), String::from_utf8_lossy(text).into_owned())) .collect(), body: String::from_utf8_lossy(payload).into_owned(), }; serde_json::to_writer(value, &line).map_err(|err| SealError::Encode(Box::new(err))) } } /// Reads the legacy system's lines, the tenant from `meta`. #[subscriber(RedisList::new("legacy.jobs"))] async fn legacy(job: &LegacyJob, ctx: &mut Context<'_>) -> HandlerOutcome { let tenant = ctx.headers().get_str("tenant").unwrap_or("unknown"); tracing::info!(job.order, tenant, "legacy job run"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } fn legacy_app() -> impl App { // The legacy system's layout is the envelope of the whole broker. RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("legacy", "0.1.0")).with_broker( RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379").envelope(MetaLine), |b| b.include(legacy), ) } examples/manual/redis_subscriptions_envelopes.rs /// One JSON line with the headers under `meta` and the payload as text under `body`: the layout /// a legacy system on the same list writes. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)] struct MetaLine; #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)] struct Line { meta: BTreeMap<String, String>, body: String, } impl Envelope for MetaLine { const CONTENT_TYPE: &'static str = "application/json"; fn locate(&self, value: &[u8]) -> Location { serde_json::from_slice::<Line>(value).map_or(Location::Bare, |line| { Location::Decoded(line.body.into_bytes()) }) } fn headers(&self, value: &[u8]) -> Option<HeaderMap> { let line = serde_json::from_slice::<Line>(value).ok()?; let mut headers = HeaderMap::new(); for (name, text) in line.meta { headers.insert(name, text); } Some(headers) } fn seal( &self, payload: &[u8], headers: &HeaderMap, value: &mut Vec<u8>, ) -> Result<(), SealError> { let line = Line { meta: headers .iter() .map(|(name, text)| (name.to_owned(), String::from_utf8_lossy(text).into_owned())) .collect(), body: String::from_utf8_lossy(payload).into_owned(), }; serde_json::to_writer(value, &line).map_err(|err| SealError::Encode(Box::new(err))) } } /// Reads the legacy system's lines, the tenant from `meta`. struct Legacy; impl Handle<LegacyJob> for Legacy { fn handle( &self, job: &LegacyJob, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { let tenant = ctx.headers().get_str("tenant").unwrap_or("unknown"); tracing::info!(job.order, tenant, "legacy job run"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn legacy_app() -> impl App { // The legacy system's layout is the envelope of the whole broker. RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("legacy", "0.1.0")).with_broker( RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379").envelope(MetaLine), |b| { let jobs = RedisList::new("legacy.jobs"); b.include(subscriber(jobs, Legacy).build()) }, ) }

TestApp::start runs the service's app on RedisBroker connected to a Redis modelled in process, groups, lists and channels included. A test hands the harness the app main runs, unchanged, and addresses the broker by its production type, tb.broker::<RedisBroker>(). The testing feature in [dev-dependencies] adds the in-process mode, and turns on the core's harness with it. The connected broker is the production one. Every command it sends, a publish, a group read, an acknowledgement, a delay-queue sweep, reaches the model as that command and is answered as Redis answers it. The model reads every setting off the broker. Its address is parsed as the connect parses it, and the pool size, the default group and the cluster topology carry over. It answers as Redis 8.4, so a claiming subscription mounts. It keeps key types: a write or a read of the wrong type fails with WRONGTYPE. It keeps consumer groups with their cursor, pending entries and delivery counts, the group's start_id, XAUTOCLAIM and XREADGROUP ... CLAIM at their idle thresholds, and a seek. It keeps lists with the processing list and its recovery set, sorted sets, key expiry and MULTI / EXEC. Pub/Sub channels, globs and sharded channels deliver to the subscriptions open at that moment and store nothing for one that is not. On a cluster topology it refuses a command or a transaction that spans hash slots. It runs no scripts: EVAL, EVALSHA, FCALL and a command it does not know fail with an error naming them. No handshake runs, so AUTH, HELLO and TLS are for a live test. A test's input goes where the default publisher writes its name: an XADD, or the LPUSH or PUBLISH of the subscription that reads the name. A publish through the harness returns once every handler it woke has settled, a reply included, so the assertions that follow read finished state. published::<T>(name) reads every write to the name back, a requeued copy and an entry a delay queue adds back included. The model's time is the test's clock: entry ids, idle times and the scores of the delay queue and the recovery set stand still on a paused clock, and tb.advance(by) moves them. A handler's own commands, through FredPool or a pipeline window, reach the model too.

The dependency line: [dev-dependencies] ruststream-fred = { version = "0.8", features = ["testing"] } The first test publishes a payment and reads how the handler settled it. Macros Manual examples/redis_testing.rs #[tokio::test] async fn a_paid_payment_is_accepted() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { let tb = TestApp::start(app()).await?; let payment = Payment { id: 1, amount: 100 }; tb.broker::<RedisBroker>() .message(&payment) .publish() .await?; tb.broker::<RedisBroker>() .subscriber("payments") .assert_called_once() .with(&payment) .settled(HandlerOutcome::ack()); Ok(()) } examples/manual/redis_testing.rs #[tokio::test] async fn a_paid_payment_is_accepted() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { let tb = TestApp::start(app()).await?; let payment = Payment { id: 1, amount: 100 }; tb.broker::<RedisBroker>() .message(&payment) .publish() .await?; tb.broker::<RedisBroker>() .subscriber("payments") .assert_called_once() .with(&payment) .settled(HandlerOutcome::ack()); Ok(()) } A settlement is answered with a receipt on the stream receipts, and the test reads the receipt back. Macros Manual examples/redis_testing.rs #[tokio::test] async fn a_settlement_is_answered_with_a_receipt() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { let tb = TestApp::start(app()).await?; tb.broker::<RedisBroker>() .message(&Settlement { id: 3 }) .publish() .await?; tb.broker::<RedisBroker>() .published::<Receipt>("receipts") .assert_called_once() .with(&Receipt { id: 3 }); Ok(()) } examples/manual/redis_testing.rs #[tokio::test] async fn a_settlement_is_answered_with_a_receipt() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { let tb = TestApp::start(app()).await?; tb.broker::<RedisBroker>() .message(&Settlement { id: 3 }) .publish() .await?; tb.broker::<RedisBroker>() .published::<Receipt>("receipts") .assert_called_once() .with(&Receipt { id: 3 }); Ok(()) } The model's time is the test's clock. Entry ids, idle times and the scores of a delay queue stand still on a paused clock, and tb.advance(by) moves them. A declined invoice comes back once the clock has moved past its delay. Macros Manual examples/redis_testing.rs #[tokio::test(start_paused = true)] async fn a_declined_invoice_comes_back_after_the_delay() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { let tb = TestApp::start(app()).await?; tb.broker::<RedisBroker>() .message(&Invoice { id: 4 }) .publish() .await?; tb.broker::<RedisBroker>() .subscriber("invoices") .assert_called_once() .settled(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RETRY_DELAY)); // The delay queue reads the test's clock, so the retry is due once the clock moves. tb.advance(RETRY_DELAY).await?; tb.broker::<RedisBroker>() .subscriber("invoices") .assert_called(2) .settled(HandlerOutcome::ack()); Ok(()) } examples/manual/redis_testing.rs #[tokio::test(start_paused = true)] async fn a_declined_invoice_comes_back_after_the_delay() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { let tb = TestApp::start(app()).await?; tb.broker::<RedisBroker>() .message(&Invoice { id: 4 }) .publish() .await?; tb.broker::<RedisBroker>() .subscriber("invoices") .assert_called_once() .settled(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RETRY_DELAY)); // The delay queue reads the test's clock, so the retry is due once the clock moves. tb.advance(RETRY_DELAY).await?; tb.broker::<RedisBroker>() .subscriber("invoices") .assert_called(2) .settled(HandlerOutcome::ack()); Ok(()) }

TestApp::start_live runs the same test body against a Redis server, for scripts, failover, authentication and TLS. It connects the broker through its ordinary connect, so the client dials the server, logs in and runs the handshake. The body is the one an in-process test runs; only the start call differs. A publish, settle and advance wait on the real clock until every subscription has handled what was published to it. The wait lasts ten seconds at most, and start_live_within sets another bound. The live mode is for what the in-process Redis leaves out: Lua scripts and functions, a cluster under resharding, a sentinel failover, authentication and TLS. A server keeps what earlier runs left in it, so a run reads keys no other test writes. In the example, live::url returns the server's address from REDIS_TEST_URL, and the test returns early without one, so cargo test passes on a machine with no server. A job that stood a server up sets RUSTSTREAM_REQUIRE_LIVE=1, and a missing address then fails the test instead of skipping it. The repository's stand is docker-compose.test.yml, which just brokers-up starts. just test-brokers starts it, runs every suite against it with RUSTSTREAM_REQUIRE_LIVE=1, and stops it. Each topology has a variable of its own: Variable Server Stand address REDIS_TEST_URL a standalone Redis 7 redis://127.0.0.1:6379 REDIS_84_TEST_URL a standalone Redis 8.4, for claiming redis://127.0.0.1:6386 REDIS_AUTH_TEST_URL a password-protected Redis 7 with an ACL user redis://127.0.0.1:6385 REDIS_CLUSTER_TEST_URL a seed node of a cluster 127.0.0.1:7000 REDIS_SENTINEL_TEST_URL a sentinel watching the primary mymaster 127.0.0.1:26379

The two tests share one body: one in process, one against the server at REDIS_TEST_URL. Macros Manual examples/redis_testing_live.rs /// The body both modes run; only the start call differs. async fn accepts_a_payment(tb: TestApp<()>) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { tb.broker::<RedisBroker>() .message(&Payment { amount: 100 }) .publish() .await?; tb.broker::<RedisBroker>() .subscriber("testing-live.payments") .assert_called_once() .with(&Payment { amount: 100 }) .settled(HandlerOutcome::ack()); tb.shutdown().await?; Ok(()) } #[tokio::test] async fn in_process() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { accepts_a_payment(TestApp::start(app("redis://localhost:6379")).await?).await } #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)] async fn against_the_server() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { let Some(url) = live::url("REDIS_TEST_URL") else { return Ok(()); }; accepts_a_payment(TestApp::start_live(app(&url)).await?).await } examples/manual/redis_testing_live.rs /// The body both modes run; only the start call differs. async fn accepts_a_payment(tb: TestApp<()>) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { tb.broker::<RedisBroker>() .message(&Payment { amount: 100 }) .publish() .await?; tb.broker::<RedisBroker>() .subscriber("testing-live.payments") .assert_called_once() .with(&Payment { amount: 100 }) .settled(HandlerOutcome::ack()); tb.shutdown().await?; Ok(()) } #[tokio::test] async fn in_process() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { accepts_a_payment(TestApp::start(app("redis://localhost:6379")).await?).await } #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)] async fn against_the_server() -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error>> { let Some(url) = live::url("REDIS_TEST_URL") else { return Ok(()); }; accepts_a_payment(TestApp::start_live(app(&url)).await?).await }

A stream publisher sends a group of publishes as one MULTI and EXEC block; a batch's replies commit together with .transactional(). The stream publisher, RedisPublisher, buffers the publishes of a transaction and sends them on commit, in publish order. Subscribers then see the whole group or none of it. It offers both kinds of transaction the framework defines. A mount that publishes in transactions names RedisTransactionalPublish, TransactionalPublish in the stream prelude, which pairs into the same publisher. This page is the borrowed kind; transaction and owned_transaction are the owned kind. The borrowed kind is the core's TransactionalPublisher: one transaction on the publisher handle. begin_transaction starts buffering, commit flushes the buffer, abort discards it, and a clone of the handle works with the same open transaction. A second begin_transaction while one is open returns RedisError::TransactionBusy and leaves the open one alone. A commit or an abort with nothing open returns RedisError::NoTransaction. Its usual shape is a batch handler whose replies commit together: .transactional() after .out_reply(TransactionalPublish) asks for it, and a policy without transactions does not compile there. Transactions run on standalone and sentinel deployments. A MULTI block cannot span hash slots, so on a cluster TransactionalPublish refuses to pair and the service does not start. The error is RedisError::InvalidOptions, raised before the service reads its first batch. Redis does not roll back: a command that fails inside EXEC leaves the commands before it committed. For a group of XADDs that happens when Redis runs out of memory or a key holds another type. A command the server refuses to queue discards the whole block instead. The list and Pub/Sub publishers send each message on its own.

Each batch's replies reach processed in one block. Macros Manual examples/redis_transactions.rs /// Processes a batch; subscribers of `processed` see all of its replies or none. #[subscriber(RedisStream::new("orders").group("workers"), reply)] async fn process(orders: &[Order]) -> Result<Vec<Processed>, HandlerOutcome> { tracing::info!(orders = orders.len(), "batch processed"); Ok(orders .iter() .map(|order| Processed { order_id: order.id }) .collect()) } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { let broker = RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(process.batch(nonzero!(32))) .out_reply(TransactionalPublish) .transactional() }) } examples/manual/redis_transactions.rs /// Processes a batch; subscribers of `processed` see all of its replies or none. struct Process; impl Handle<[Order], Vec<Processed>> for Process { fn handle( &self, orders: &[Order], _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Vec<Processed>, Vec<HandlerOutcome>>> { tracing::info!(orders = orders.len(), "batch processed"); ready(Ok(orders .iter() .map(|order| Processed { order_id: order.id }) .collect())) } } fn app() -> impl App { let broker = RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { let process = subscriber(RedisStream::new("orders").group("workers"), Process); b.include(process.batch(nonzero!(32)).reply().build()) .out_reply(TransactionalPublish) .transactional() }) }

owned_transaction is the same buffer over values, encoding each one with the default codec. It is the owned kind on a live publisher outside a handler, where no slot carries a codec: the publisher an after_startup hook is handed, for one. publisher.owned_transaction() returns a TypedTransaction that owns its buffer. publish(name, &value) encodes the value and buffers it; commit sends the buffer as one MULTI / EXEC block, and abort discards it. As with transaction, any number can be open on one publisher, and commit and abort consume the value. after_startup runs its hook once the broker is connected and the subscriptions are open, with the policy it names paired into a live publisher. That makes it the place for a service's first publishes, such as seed data that must arrive whole. A hook that returns an error fails the startup. On a cluster TransactionalPublish refuses to pair, so the service does not start and seeds nothing.

The service writes its opening prices as one block once it is connected; the catalog reader sees both or neither. Macros Manual examples/redis_transactions_owned.rs /// Writes the opening prices as one block: readers of `prices` see the whole list or none of it. async fn seed_prices<P: OwnedTransactions>( publisher: P, ) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>> { let mut seed = publisher.owned_transaction().await?; for (sku, cents) in [("tea", 450), ("cake", 600)] { let price = Price { sku: sku.to_owned(), cents, }; seed.publish("prices", &price).await?; } seed.commit().await?; Ok(()) } /// The service on `broker`: a standalone or a sentinel deployment, where `MULTI` / `EXEC` runs. fn app_on(broker: RedisBroker) -> impl App<State = ()> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("catalog", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { // Runs once the broker is connected and the subscription is open. b.after_startup(TransactionalPublish, async move |publisher| { seed_prices(publisher).await.map_err(io::Error::other) }) .include(list_price) }) } examples/manual/redis_transactions_owned.rs /// Writes the opening prices as one block: readers of `prices` see the whole list or none of it. async fn seed_prices<P: OwnedTransactions>( publisher: P, ) -> Result<(), Box<dyn Error + Send + Sync>> { let mut seed = publisher.owned_transaction().await?; for (sku, cents) in [("tea", 450), ("cake", 600)] { let price = Price { sku: sku.to_owned(), cents, }; seed.publish("prices", &price).await?; } seed.commit().await?; Ok(()) } /// The service on `broker`: a standalone or a sentinel deployment, where `MULTI` / `EXEC` runs. fn app_on(broker: RedisBroker) -> impl App<State = ()> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("catalog", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { let list_price = subscriber(RedisStream::new("prices").group("catalog"), ListPrice); // Runs once the broker is connected and the subscription is open. b.after_startup(TransactionalPublish, async move |publisher| { seed_prices(publisher).await.map_err(io::Error::other) }) .include(list_price.build()) }) }

transaction hands back a value that owns its buffer, so several can be open at once and a double commit does not compile. This is the owned kind, the core's OwnedTransactions. A handler takes its slot as Out<impl OwnedTransactions, Slot> and calls transaction() on it. The value it gets back publishes like the slot, txn.message(&value).publish(), and admits the types the slot admits. Each call opens a buffer of its own, so the workers of a workers(n) subscription never share one, and the slot keeps publishing directly meanwhile. commit sends the buffer as one MULTI / EXEC block; abort discards it. Both consume the value, so a second commit or a publish after settling does not compile. Dropping a transaction that was neither committed nor aborted discards its buffer, as an abort does, and writes a warning. A commit that fails has consumed the transaction, and its buffer is gone. The recovery is to redeliver the input, which a retry outcome does, not to send the buffer again. The live transaction is a RedisTransaction, with the same limits as the borrowed kind: standalone and sentinel only, no rollback. The slot's policy is TransactionalPublish, so a cluster refuses it at startup.

An order ships one entry per item in one block, on four workers at once; an item without a name aborts the transaction, which discards the entries already buffered. Macros Manual examples/redis_transactions_transaction.rs /// One shipment per item, committed as one block; four orders ship at once. #[subscriber(RedisStream::new("orders").group("shipping"), workers(4))] async fn ship( order: &Order, Out(shipments): Out<impl OwnedTransactions, Shipments>, ) -> HandlerOutcome { let Ok(mut txn) = shipments.transaction().await else { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); }; for item in &order.items { if item.is_empty() { tracing::warn!(order.id, "an item has no name, the order ships nothing"); // The abort discards the shipments the transaction buffered so far. return match txn.abort().await { Ok(()) => HandlerOutcome::drop(), Err(_) => HandlerOutcome::retry(), }; } let shipment = Shipment { order_id: order.id, item: item.clone(), }; if txn.message(&shipment).publish().await.is_err() { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } } match txn.commit().await { Ok(()) => HandlerOutcome::ack(), Err(_) => HandlerOutcome::retry(), } } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shipping", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379"), |b| { b.include(ship).out(Shipments, TransactionalPublish) }) } examples/manual/redis_transactions_transaction.rs /// One shipment per item, committed as one block; four orders ship at once. struct Ship; impl<S> Handle<Order, (), Outs<(S,)>> for Ship where S: OutEntry<Shipments, Wire: OwnedTransactions>, { async fn handle( &self, order: &Order, outs: &Outs<(S,)>, _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let mut txn = outs .get(Shipments) .transaction() .await .map_err(|_| HandlerOutcome::retry())?; for item in &order.items { if item.is_empty() { tracing::warn!(order.id, "an item has no name, the order ships nothing"); // The abort discards the shipments the transaction buffered so far. txn.abort().await.map_err(|_| HandlerOutcome::retry())?; return Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()); } let shipment = Shipment { order_id: order.id, item: item.clone(), }; txn.message(&shipment) .publish() .await .map_err(|_| HandlerOutcome::retry())?; } txn.commit().await.map_err(|_| HandlerOutcome::retry()) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shipping", "0.1.0")).with_broker( RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379"), |b| { let ship = subscriber(RedisStream::new("orders").group("shipping"), Ship); b.include(ship.workers(nonzero!(4)).build()) .out(Shipments, TransactionalPublish) }, ) }

Это руководство сравнивает три структуры Redis, которые читает сервис: поток, список и канал Pub/Sub. Пример - сервис магазина, который работает со всеми тремя. Счета по заказам выставляются из потока, миниатюры строятся из списка, а изменения цен приходят по каналу.

Макросы Вручную src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "orders")] struct Order { id: u64, amount_cents: u64, } #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "invoices")] struct Invoice { order_id: u64, amount_cents: u64, } #[subscriber(RedisStream::new("orders").group("billing"), reply)] async fn bill(order: &Order) -> Invoice { tracing::info!(order.id, "order billed"); Invoice { order_id: order.id, amount_cents: order.amount_cents, } } src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Order { id: u64, amount_cents: u64, } #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Invoice { order_id: u64, amount_cents: u64, } named!(Order, "orders"); named!(Invoice, "invoices"); struct Bill; impl Handle<Order, Invoice> for Bill { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Invoice, HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order billed"); ready(Ok(Invoice { order_id: order.id, amount_cents: order.amount_cents, })) } } Поток Redis хранит каждую запись, пока сервис её не обрежет. RedisStream читает поток через группу потребителей. Каждая группа получает каждую запись один раз, а внутри группы её обрабатывает один потребитель. Подтверждённая запись получает XACK. Запись, которую потребитель не подтвердил, остаётся в списке неподтверждённых записей группы, поэтому сбой ничего не теряет. Поток можно прочитать заново с более ранней записи через перемотку. Заказы - это деньги, поэтому они идут через поток. bill отвечает на каждый заказ счётом Invoice, который попадает в поток invoices.

Макросы Вручную src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "thumbnails")] struct Thumbnail { image: String, } #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "thumbnails.ready")] struct ThumbnailReady { image: String, } #[subscriber(RedisList::new("thumbnails").reliable(), reply)] async fn render(job: &Thumbnail) -> ThumbnailReady { tracing::info!(job.image, "thumbnail rendered"); ThumbnailReady { image: job.image.clone(), } } src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Thumbnail { image: String, } #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct ThumbnailReady { image: String, } named!(Thumbnail, "thumbnails"); named!(ThumbnailReady, "thumbnails.ready"); struct Render; impl Handle<Thumbnail, ThumbnailReady> for Render { fn handle( &self, job: &Thumbnail, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<ThumbnailReady, HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(job.image, "thumbnail rendered"); ready(Ok(ThumbnailReady { image: job.image.clone(), })) } } Список Redis - это очередь: производитель добавляет запись, и ровно один потребитель её извлекает. RedisList::new извлекает запись командой BRPOP. Запись покидает Redis до запуска обработчика, и сбой в обработчике её теряет. reliable вместо этого переносит запись в список обработки и удаляет её только после подтверждения обработчиком. У списка нет групп и нет повторного чтения. Построение миниатюры - работа для одного воркера, поэтому задания идут через надёжный список. render объявляет о каждой готовой миниатюре в канале thumbnails.ready.

Макросы Вручную src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "prices")] struct PriceChange { sku: String, price_cents: u64, } #[subscriber(RedisPubSub::new("prices"))] async fn refresh_price(change: &PriceChange) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(change.sku, change.price_cents, "price cache refreshed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct PriceChange { sku: String, price_cents: u64, } named!(PriceChange, "prices"); struct RefreshPrice; impl Handle<PriceChange> for RefreshPrice { fn handle( &self, change: &PriceChange, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(change.sku, change.price_cents, "price cache refreshed"); ready(Ok(())) } } Сообщение Pub/Sub получает каждый подписчик, подключённый в момент публикации. Redis ничего не хранит: подписчик, который не подключён, сообщение не увидит. У RedisPubSub нет подтверждения, поэтому исход, который возвращает обработчик, ничего не завершает. Изменение цены важно только экземплярам, которые работают сейчас и обновляют свой кеш, поэтому оно идёт через канал.

Поток Список Pub/Sub Хранится, пока никто не читает пока не обрезан пока не извлечён нет Кто получает сообщение один потребитель в каждой группе один потребитель каждый подключённый подписчик ack XACK надёжный: LREM из списка обработки; простой: ничего ничего retry копия, добавленная в поток надёжный: обратно в список; простой: теряется теряется retry_after копия после задержки копия после задержки копия после задержки Пакет одно чтение до n записей собирает клиент собирает клиент Повторное чтение перемотка группы нет нет Страницы о подтверждении описывают каждый исход полностью, а руководство Переобработка, задержки и dead-letter показывает, как работают задержка и предел попыток на каждой структуре. Пакет на потоке - это COUNT одного чтения. Список и канал доставляют по одной записи, поэтому пакет того же размера собирает клиент. Одно имя занимает одна структура. Поток и список - это ключи определённого типа, и запись другого типа возвращает ошибку WRONGTYPE. Канал вообще не ключ: XADD под именем канала создаёт поток, которого подписчики канала никогда не увидят.

Макросы Вручную src/main.rs #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shop", "0.1.0")).with_broker( RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379"), |b| { b.include(bill) .out_reply(stream::Publish) .include(render) .out_reply(pubsub::Publish::default()) .include(refresh_price) }, ) } src/main.rs fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shop", "0.1.0")).with_broker( RedisBroker::standalone("redis://localhost:6379"), |b| { b.include( subscriber(RedisStream::new("orders").group("billing"), Bill) .reply() .build(), ) .out_reply(stream::Publish) .include( subscriber(RedisList::new("thumbnails").reliable(), Render) .reply() .build(), ) .out_reply(pubsub::Publish::default()) .include(subscriber(RedisPubSub::new("prices"), RefreshPrice).build()) }, ) } fn main() -> ExitCode { run_main(app) } Сервис на одном транспорте импортирует прелюдию этого транспорта, например ruststream_fred::stream::prelude. Этот сервис сочетает транспорты, поэтому импортирует ruststream_fred::prelude. В ней политика публикации каждого транспорта сохраняет имя своего модуля: stream::Publish пишет командой XADD, pubsub::Publish командой PUBLISH. Тип ответа задаёт, куда уходит ответ, а политика в точке монтирования задаёт, как он туда попадает. Три обработчика устроены одинаково. Чтобы перенести обработчик на другой транспорт, меняют дескриптор в его атрибуте и политику в его точке монтирования, а тело остаётся прежним. Тесты в файле примера публикуют в каждый транспорт и читают то, что отправили в ответ обработчики, и всё это внутри процесса.

Это руководство запускает сервис на Redis Cluster и даёт ключам имена так, чтобы ключи одной команды находились в одном хеш-слоте. Пример - серверная часть магазина. Она выполняет задания из очереди заданий, выставляет счета по заказам из потока и слушает события в шардированном канале.

Макросы Вручную src/main.rs fn service(broker: RedisBroker) -> impl App<State = ()> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shop", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(run_job) .include(invoice.pipeline().atomic()) .include(on_event) }) } /// Two seeds: the client reaches the cluster through whichever answers first. #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { service(RedisBroker::cluster([ "redis-1.internal:6379", "redis-2.internal:6379", ])) } src/main.rs fn service(broker: RedisBroker) -> impl App<State = ()> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("shop", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { let invoice = subscriber(RedisStream::new("{orders}").group("billing"), Invoice); let events = RedisPubSub::new("events").mode(PubSubMode::Sharded); b.include(subscriber(RedisList::new("{jobs}").reliable(), RunJob).build()) .include(invoice.pipeline().atomic().build()) .include(subscriber(events, OnEvent).build()) }) } /// Two seeds: the client reaches the cluster through whichever answers first. fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { service(RedisBroker::cluster([ "redis-1.internal:6379", "redis-2.internal:6379", ])) } fn main() -> ExitCode { run_main(app) } RedisBroker::cluster принимает начальные узлы. Достаточно одного доступного узла: клиент читает с него устройство кластера и подключается к каждому ведущему узлу. Как и любой конструктор брокера, этот не выполняет ввода-вывода. Соединение открывается при запуске сервиса. Обработчики одинаковы на одиночном сервере и в кластере. Меняется то, как сервис называет свои ключи.

Кластер распределяет ключи по 16384 хеш-слотам, и каждый ведущий узел владеет их диапазоном. Команда, блок MULTI или скрипт, которые затрагивают несколько ключей, выполняются, только если все ключи находятся в одном слоте. Слот определяет хеш-тег: если в ключе есть часть в фигурных скобках, хешируется только она. {jobs} и {jobs}.processing находятся в одном слоте, как и {orders} и {orders}:invoices. Имя в фигурных скобках не может быть постоянным местом назначения типа, потому что #[outgoing(name = "..")] читает фигурные скобки как шаблон имени. Производитель задаёт такой ключ там, где публикует: .message(&job).to("{jobs}").

Макросы Вручную src/main.rs /// The hash tag `{jobs}` keeps the queue and its processing list `{jobs}.processing` on one slot. #[subscriber(RedisList::new("{jobs}").reliable())] async fn run_job(job: &Job) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(job.id, "job done"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs /// The hash tag `{jobs}` keeps the queue and its processing list `{jobs}.processing` on one slot. struct RunJob; impl Handle<Job> for RunJob { fn handle( &self, job: &Job, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(job.id, "job done"); ready(Ok(())) } } Надёжный список переносит каждую запись в список обработки одной командой LMOVE, поэтому оба ключа должны находиться в одном слоте. Список обработки называется как очередь с добавленным .processing и сохраняет хеш-тег очереди. Надёжный список, два ключа которого попадают в разные слоты, не запускается, а ошибка называет хеш-тег, который нужно использовать.

Макросы Вручную src/main.rs /// Invoices an order; the invoice and the acknowledgement commit as one block on the slot of /// `{orders}`. #[subscriber(RedisStream::new("{orders}").group("billing"))] async fn invoice(order: &Order, Ctx(pipeline): Ctx<keys::Pipeline>) -> HandlerOutcome { if pipeline .lpush("{orders}:invoices", order.id.to_string()) .await .is_err() { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs /// Invoices an order; the invoice and the acknowledgement commit as one block on the slot of /// `{orders}`. struct Invoice; impl Handle<Order, (), (), PipelineContext> for Invoice { async fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_, PipelineContext>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { ctx.context(keys::Pipeline) .lpush("{orders}:invoices", order.id.to_string()) .await .map_err(|_| HandlerOutcome::retry()) } } Поток - это один ключ, поэтому подписка на поток работает под любым именем. Атомарное окно помещает команды обработчика и XACK в один блок MULTI, и блок выполняется в слоте потока. invoice пишет в {orders}:invoices, в слот потока {orders}. Команда для ключа в другом слоте заставляет Redis отклонить весь блок: ничего не записывается, и запись потока остаётся неподтверждённой. Транзакция издателя потока - тоже блок MULTI, и её места назначения не привязаны к одному слоту. Поэтому на кластере сервис с политикой TransactionalPublish не запускается.

Макросы Вручную src/main.rs /// Sharded Pub/Sub: the channel lives on the node that owns its slot. #[subscriber(RedisPubSub::new("events").mode(PubSubMode::Sharded))] async fn on_event(event: &Event) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(event.kind, "event received"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs /// Sharded Pub/Sub: the channel lives on the node that owns its slot. struct OnEvent; impl Handle<Event> for OnEvent { fn handle( &self, event: &Event, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(event.kind, "event received"); ready(Ok(())) } } Классический Pub/Sub в кластере отправляет каждое сообщение на каждый узел. PubSubMode::Sharded отправляет его только на узел, которому принадлежит слот канала, командами SPUBLISH и SSUBSCRIBE, поэтому трафик масштабируется вместе с кластером. Этому режиму нужен Redis 7 или новее. Два режима не видят друг друга: шардированное сообщение никогда не доходит до классического подписчика, и наоборот. Издатель канала использует режим подписки. Подписка по шаблону бывает только классической.

Тесты запускают промышленное приложение через TestApp::start с брокером кластера. Redis внутри процесса ведёт себя как кластер: он отклоняет команду или блок, которые охватывают несколько хеш-слотов. Поэтому тесты проверяют, что каждая форма работает с хеш-тегами сервиса, что надёжный список без тега не запускается и что блок на два слота ничего не фиксирует. То же тело теста работает с настоящим кластером, когда REDIS_CLUSTER_TEST_URL называет его узел. Переключение при отказе и перераспределение слотов бывают только на настоящем кластере. Что брокер делает в этих случаях, описывает руководство по промышленной эксплуатации.

Это руководство делит поток Redis между воркерами и между сервисами и возвращает в работу записи, которые не закончил остановившийся воркер. Пример - платёжный сервис. Платежи приходят в поток payments. Группа бухгалтерского журнала проводит каждый платёж, а группа антифрода его проверяет.
documents.s: Группы потребителей и восстановление после сбоя

documents.t: Макросы Вручную src/main.rs /// Longer than the slowest posting ever takes: an entry idle this long belongs to no live worker. const MIN_IDLE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30); #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "payments")] struct Payment { id: u64, account: String, amount_cents: u64, } #[subscriber( RedisStream::claiming("payments", MIN_IDLE).group("ledger"), workers(8, by_key) )] async fn post_payment(payment: &Payment, ctx: &mut Context<'_>) -> HandlerOutcome { let earlier_deliveries = ctx.headers().get_str(DELIVERY_COUNT_HEADER).unwrap_or("0"); if payment.account.starts_with("migrating-") { tracing::warn!( payment.id, earlier_deliveries, "account locked, payment left pending" ); return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } tracing::info!(payment.id, earlier_deliveries, "payment posted"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs /// Longer than the slowest posting ever takes: an entry idle this long belongs to no live worker. const MIN_IDLE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30); #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Payment { id: u64, account: String, amount_cents: u64, } named!(Payment, "payments"); struct PostPayment; impl Handle<Payment> for PostPayment { fn handle( &self, payment: &Payment, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { let earlier_deliveries = ctx.headers().get_str(DELIVERY_COUNT_HEADER).unwrap_or("0"); if payment.account.starts_with("migrating-") { tracing::warn!( payment.id, earlier_deliveries, "account locked, payment left pending" ); return ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::retry())); } tracing::info!(payment.id, earlier_deliveries, "payment posted"); ready(Ok(())) } } Поток Redis читается через группу потребителей. Группа хранит курсор в потоке, и каждая запись за курсором достаётся одному потребителю группы. Каждая подписка - это один потребитель. Поэтому каждый работающий экземпляр сервиса добавляет потребителя в ledger, и экземпляры делят платежи между собой. Потребитель получает сгенерированное имя: ruststream-0, ruststream-1 и так далее в каждом процессе. consumer задаёт имя, например по имени хоста, чтобы XINFO CONSUMERS различал экземпляры. Запись, выданная потребителю, попадает в список неподтверждённых записей группы. Она покидает этот список, когда обработчик её подтверждает. Если воркер останавливается раньше, из-за сбоя или развёртывания, запись остаётся неподтверждённой: Redis хранит её, и сам он не передаёт её другому потребителю. RedisStream::claiming читает оба набора за один вызов: сначала записи, которые ждут подтверждения не меньше min_idle, затем новые.
